summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after awakening with severe substernal chest pain radiating to her back, diagnosed with a Type A aortic dissection involving the ascending and descending aorta. She underwent emergent ascending aortic and hemiarch graft replacement, followed by reoperation for postoperative bleeding with temporary chest closure. She experienced complications including heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, bilateral upper extremity deep vein thromboses, postoperative atrial fibrillation requiring cardioversion, and acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with pulmonary edema requiring aggressive diuresis and ventilator support. A urinary tract infection was treated with oral ciprofloxacin, and a new left knee effusion was evaluated but found not to be septic. She was successfully weaned off the ventilator by postoperative day 9, transitioned to oral intake, and transferred to a step-down unit. By discharge, she was ambulating steadily, alert, and managing pain with oral medications. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with a plan for outpatient MRA of the aorta with premedication for contrast allergy.
